title: Resurrection
english: A helpless man is free even among the dead.
The same one who spoke earlier now says in the 74th Psalm, 'Arise, God, judge the earth' (Psalm 74:7).
Isaiah also speaks of a great shepherd who will be brought up from the earth (Isaiah 40:11).
Nahum, meanwhile, describes the feet of the one who evangelizes peace as swift on the mountains (Nahum 1:15).
The soldiers who guard the tomb will do so in vain, for as David says in the 75th Psalm, 'They slept their sleep and did not find anything' (Psalm 75:5).
The resurrection will come in the morning, as David says in the 76th Psalm, 'Weeping will lodge in the evening and joy in the morning' (Psalm 76:5).
David also says in the 76th Psalm, 'I cried out to you, Lord, and my prayer will precede you in the morning' (Psalm 76:6).
And in the 79th Psalm, 'Arise, lyre and harp; I will arise at dawn' (Psalm 79:6).

The place of the resurrection will be a testimony, as Nahum says, 'Prepare, rise, all their foliage has withered; therefore wait for me, says the Lord, for the day of my resurrection, for my testimony; for my judgment will bring all my enemies' (Nahum 1:5-6).
In the Songs, it is written, 'Arise, come, my neighbor, in the shadow of the rock, beside the fortification' (Song of Solomon 2:14), indicating that the women will seek him.
But he will first meet the women, as the Songs also say, 'I found the one my soul loved, I grasped him and did not let him go' (Song of Solomon 3:4).
And they will depart in fear, as David says in the 2nd Psalm, 'You should serve the Lord in fear and rejoice in Him with trembling' (Psalm 2:11).
Isaiah says, 'Women are coming from seeing, come; for the people do not have understanding' (Isaiah 27:11).
The Spirit will be breathed into the apostles, as Nahum prophesies, saying, 'Prepare, rise, for all their undergrowth has perished' (Nahum 1:4), and the breath has gone up into their face.
In the Songs, it is said, 'I ate my bread with my honey' (Song of Solomon 5:1), indicating that the bitter experience of the passion will be followed by the sweetness of the resurrection.
Jonah says, 'Guarding vainly and false pity, they abandoned' (Jonah 2:8).
And Isaiah says, 'But say to us and announce to us another deception' (Isaiah 41:21-24).

The dead will rise, as Hosea says, 'They will rise early, saying, Let us go and return to the Lord, for He has struck and healed us, struck and made us healthy after two days, and on the third day we will rise before Him' (Hosea 6:1-3).
And Isaiah says, 'The dead will rise, and those in the tombs will be raised, and those on the earth will rejoice' (Isaiah 26:19).
Zechariah says, 'And you, in the blood of the covenant, sent your prisoners from the pit having no water' (Zechariah 9:11).
And Hosea says, 'I will rescue them from the hand of Hades, and I will redeem them from death; where is your judgment, O death? Where is your sting, O Hades?' (Hosea 13:14).

Ezekiel says, 'Thus says the Lord: I open your tombs and bring you up out of your tombs and lead you into the land of Israel, and you will know that I am the Lord when I open your graves' (Ezekiel 37:12-13).
translator_notes: The Greek text may be fragmented, and some sentences may be cut off at the end.
The translation of 'ἄνθρωπος ἀβοήθητος' as 'a helpless man' is literal, but the phrase 'ἐν νεκροῖς ἐλεύθερος' is translated idiomatically as 'free among the dead'.
The allusion to Ezekiel 37:12-13 is noted.
The last sentence of the source is not fully preserved, but it seems to end with a reference to Ezekiel 37:12-13.
